description.purpose: Recommend Washington Reagan National for a National Mall stay by comparing the returned airport distances and ground travel times, price a nonstop PHX-DCA round trip (October 14 to 19) in standard economy for the caller and her 12-year-old grandson with two checked bags, a free folding walker and optional insurance, verify her identity, validate her 200 dollar certificate, and book reservation B9RT6M with the remainder on her Visa ending 1182.
description.notes: Every figure (the one-stop saving, the fare with bags, insurance, the walker's treatment, the certificate value) must come from the tools before it is spoken. Identity must be verified before stored cards or certificates are used, and the agent must not paraphrase ID or custody rules for the minor or promise seats.

user_scenario.persona: A warm, slightly hesitant grandmother who laughs at herself, sometimes misses what was said, and double-checks details like dates, codes and totals before she is satisfied.

instructions.reason_for_call: You want to book a round trip from Phoenix to Washington for yourself and your grandson, but the website shows three different Washington airports and you do not know which one you need.
instructions.known_info:
You are Linda Marie Carver (Carver spelled C-A-R-V-E-R), born March 8, 1954.
Your grandson is Evan James Carver, born July 21, 2014. He is 12 years old.
You are staying near the National Mall.
You want to leave October 14 and come back October 19.
Your contact email is linda.carver9@outlook.com.
You think there is a Visa ending in 1182 already on your account.
You have a travel certificate for 200 dollars with code CT-449108 (say it as C-T-449108).
You will each check one suitcase, and you travel with a folding walker.
Your grandson's mother is not traveling, and he does not have a driver's license.
instructions.unknown_info: You do not know which Washington airport is best, the flight times, the fares, whether the walker costs extra, or the insurance price.
instructions.task_instructions:
Say you are trying to book from Phoenix to Washington for you and your grandson, and the website shows three airports and you do not know which you need. When asked, say you are staying near the National Mall, and give your travel dates. Accept the airport the agent recommends and say you need nonstop, that you are traveling with your 12-year-old grandson, and that you have a folding walker. When told about basic versus standard fares, say you definitely need standard because you have to sit together. If offered a one-stop comparison, agree as long as it is not a five-hour layover; when you hear the saving, say it is not worth it, choose nonstop, and say you will each check one suitcase plus the walker. When the price and insurance are quoted, ask the agent to go ahead and add the insurance.

Give names, birthdates and email when asked. Say you should have a Visa ending in 1182 on the account and a 200 dollar travel certificate; give the code when asked and confirm the readback. After booking, repeat the confirmation code back as B9RT6M to check it. Ask whether the certificate applied, confirm two checked bags, and ask the agent to repeat the airports. Then ask whether you need a letter from your grandson's mother since she is not traveling, and mention he does not have a driver's license. Ask what birth date they entered for him, then confirm yours. Ask whether the certificate code had a zero or the letter O. Ask whether you can choose seats now; when told to use the reservation screen, report that you see 16A and 16B outbound and 14D and 14E on return, then say confirmed. Ask whether the walker needs a serial number. Ask for the total one more time and say it matches your screen. Say you have written down the confirmation and total, thank the agent for being patient, and end the call.

nl_assertions: Agent verifies the caller's name, date of birth and email before using the stored Visa or the travel certificate.
Agent tells the caller that the folding walker does not count as paid baggage.
Agent tells the caller that the trip insurance has exclusions and that she should review the plan document.
Agent quotes the price including the two checked bags and the insurance before booking the reservation.
Agent tells the caller that 200 dollars came from the certificate and the rest was charged to the Visa ending in 1182.
Agent does not paraphrase identification or custody rules for the grandson and directs the caller to official government guidance.
